overview: Two-step plan. Step 1 (October 2026): a four-week profile of INR and dose records at the three clinics to establish whether time in therapeutic range can be calculated. Step 2 (from January 2027, only after the design decision is revisited): either a records comparison adjusted for case mix or a randomised comparison of new referrals, with the primary outcome fixed now so that it cannot drift with the design.
population: Step 1: every patient on warfarin managed by the clinic during the profile window (about 1,150). Step 2: adults starting or continuing clinic-dosed warfarin at any site, excluding patients who self-manage their dose at home.
exposure: Dose adjustment with the paper nomogram (main site) or with the computer-assisted dosing tool (satellites).
procedures: Step 1: a pharmacist extracts, for each patient, the dates of INR tests, the dates of entry where known, the doses recorded, the testing mode (clinic or home) and four case-mix variables (age, indication, interacting medicines, time on warfarin), inside the hospital network. Time in range is counted as calculable when no gap between INRs exceeds 56 days. Step 2 is specified after the decision is revisited against criterion k1.

outcomes.name: Time in therapeutic range
outcomes.measure: Percentage of days with INR in the target range, by linear interpolation between consecutive INRs, per patient
outcomes.timing: 26 weeks from the start of step 2
outcomes.why: The standard measure of dosing quality that either design can use; fixed before the design is chosen.

outcomes.name: Major bleeding or thromboembolic event
outcomes.measure: Hospital attendance for major bleeding, stroke or systemic embolism
outcomes.timing: 26 weeks from the start of step 2
outcomes.why: The outcome patients care about; too rare to power at clinic scale, so reported descriptively.

outcomes.name: Calculability of time in range
outcomes.measure: Proportion of patients with no INR gap longer than 56 days, by clinic and testing mode
outcomes.why: Decides whether the records comparison is possible (criterion k1).

outcomes.name: Pharmacist time per dosing decision
outcomes.measure: Minutes per dosing decision timed on 40 decisions per approach
outcomes.why: Standardising must not add workload the clinic cannot absorb.

feasibility: Step 1 needs about 16 hours of pharmacist time over four weeks, within the four hours a week available, under approval ACM-2026-14; the feasibility of step 2 depends on the design chosen after the profile.
biasMitigation: Primary outcome and case-mix variables fixed before any data are seen
Same extraction rules at all three clinics
The design choice is made on calculability, never on time-in-range values seen in step 1

biasFlags.label: Confounding by site case mix
biasFlags.note: Approach and site coincide; only a randomised comparison removes it.

biasFlags.label: Missing or late home INR entries
biasFlags.note: May make time in range incalculable for the patients most at risk.

biasFlags.label: Learning curve for pharmacists new to the software
biasFlags.note: Relevant only if step 2 is randomised.

flags: Step 2 left unspecified until the profile is complete
parsimony.simplestPath: Profile the records, then choose the simpler design the data allow.

theoreticalFramework: None; a data-quality profile followed by a comparative design chosen on a pre-stated rule.
summary: Records profile first, with the comparison's primary outcome fixed in advance; the design stays open by decision.
